dimension_resolution.name: cn_set
dimension_resolution.source: company_name where country_code != pl_code AND (name contains 'Film' OR 'Warner')

join_order.probe: title (year filter) -> ml -> mc -> cc -> mi
join_order.notes: sequel keyword has ~2.8k movies; drive entire pipeline from this small set
must capture cn_id to materialize MIN(cn.name)
EXISTS-style: stop at first matching mi row

filters.predicate: country_code != '[pl]' AND (name LIKE '%Film%' OR name LIKE '%Warner%')

data_structures.mc_match_state: per_t_id capture cn_id (int32) for MIN materialization
data_structures.ml_match_state: per_t_id capture lt_id (int32) for MIN materialization
data_structures.title_match_state: per_t_id capture t_id for MIN(t.title) materialization
data_structures.global_min_reducer: lexicographic compare of varlen via off+dat; tracked as (best_off, best_len) per output column

parallelism.reduction: per-thread local (min_cn_id, min_lt_id, min_t_id) ints; final pass resolves varlen MIN across thread-local candidate sets
parallelism.notes: Driver cardinality ~2800 is small but per-row work probes 5 CSR slices; parallel still worthwhile. Use atomic-free thread-local accumulators.

min_materialization.producing_company: track winning cn_id across threads; final MIN over distinct cn_ids by comparing company_name varlen
min_materialization.link_type: track winning lt_id across threads; final MIN over distinct lt_ids by comparing link_type varlen
min_materialization.complete_western_sequel: track winning t_id across threads; final MIN over distinct t_ids by comparing title varlen
min_materialization.strategy: Because each thread may see multiple candidate (cn_id, lt_id, t_id) per matching tuple, maintain a small thread-local set (or just compare-and-keep best id ordered by string lex). Final reduction: load varlen for ids, pick lex-min.
